video_title: Pablo Torre on the result of NBA’s investigation into Kawhi and the Clippers | The Rich Eisen Show

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA investigation into Clippers and Kawhi Leonard's contract
quotes.excerpt: they found an almost bottomless rabbit hole. And that's what took a year.

text_blocks.speaker: Rich Eisen
text_blocks.text: What does this ruling indicate to you, Pablo?

text_blocks.speaker: Pablo Torre
text_blocks.text: The scope that the NBA gave Lawrence Frank and their outside counsel was both specific—not everything that we reported is in their report—but within that specificity, that scope, they found an almost bottomless rabbit hole. And that's what took a year. You see in this report Aspiration, Dectronics, you see the story that we've said, thanks to frankly brave people who were willing to go on the record with me talking about the richest owner in American sports, Steve Ballmer. And what Lawrence Frank found was that there was a pattern of behavior in which Steve Ballmer and his two lieutenants, President of Basketball Lawrence Frank, President of Business Gillian Zucker, they orchestrated a scheme to use partners in the Intuit Dome like Aspiration, like Dectronics, like Locked-in Insurance, like Boingo Wireless to get Kawhi Leonard money well beyond the salary cap. In fact, so far beyond that the NBA handed out a punishment that seems to be the biggest punishment against an owner in the history of American sports.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers' vehement denial of the reporting regarding their organization
quotes.excerpt: the immediate response was, this story you're trying to tell is provably false.

text_blocks.speaker: Rich Eisen
text_blocks.text: Part of your superpower of being a terrific journalist is in order to be that, you got to put yourself in other people's shoes to see what might be happening from that point of view to try and lead to collecting data. So in that spirit, where does the Clippers' vehement response come from, do you think?

text_blocks.speaker: Pablo Torre
text_blocks.text: It's as good a question as any that's been asked this whole time. Because from the beginning, when we went to comment from the Clippers before episode one dropped, one year ago exactly today, we asked for an explanation and the immediate response was, this story you're trying to tell is provably false. Soon after, in a second round of commentary, as Steve goes on ESPN and talks to Ramona and offers this testimony that is now in the NBA's report by the way, because they fact-check and disprove those things as not true, he takes away provably false and he begins to threaten to explain what really happened here, such that this weird podcaster would be embarrassed, such that anybody who believed the sources I was relying on would be regretful in trying to tell that story.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: The NBA investigation into the Clippers' manufactured paper trail
quotes.excerpt: there's a manufactured paper trail that was meant to deceive the NBA.
quotes.quote: For a year, we've waited for the alternate rational explanation. And so when they threaten it still today, after the NBA provides this 35-page report by Wachtell Lipton which cost $50 million—that's $50 million coming out of Steve Ballmer's pocket by the way, that's how the investigation is billed as he pointed out in a letter to Adam Silver in which he threatened the thing you're alluding to—they find a level of detail and documentation and sourcing and testimony that we did not have access to, but is from Lawrence Frank who was taking contemporaneous notes, which is very interesting, which is from other emails that show that there's a manufactured paper trail that was meant to deceive the NBA.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Kawhi Leonard's punishment and the arbitration threat
quotes.excerpt: he threatens not a lawsuit. He threatens arbitration. He's going to go to arbitration.
quotes.quote: Something that the NBA had a firm grasp on that it does not seem like Steve Ballmer did. And I say this because after the punishment, the ruling is dropped, Ballmer immediately threatens not a lawsuit. He threatens arbitration. He's going to go to arbitration. What the NBA has now confirmed is that their grasp of the CBA is quite specific. They understood that the CBA makes arbitration a process that must be enacted by the player and his union. And so when Kawhi Leonard says, contra Steve Ballmer, 'Hey guys, my bad, I had an inner circle that was out of control, I regret all this, I want to move on, peace out, I'll see you in Toronto,' what he's saying is, I have settled. And he has, and the union has, meaning that arbitration is off the table. And Steve Ballmer can only go to the actual court system and sue everybody—Adam Silver, the NBA, Wachtell Lipton, me, you, whoever he wants. That's what he would be threatening.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Kawhi Leonard's fine and the settlement impact
quotes.excerpt: no suspension, no voiding, no suspension. I'll see you in Toronto. What Kawhi did was give, according to my reporting, a settlement.
quotes.quote: The reason I think that says so much about Kawhi Leonard is because by a relative slap on the wrist for Kawhi, $700,000 fine, right? No suspension, no voiding, no suspension. I'll see you in Toronto. What Kawhi did was give, according to my reporting, a settlement that ended up handicapping what Steve Ballmer could do legally. And that is fascinating.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Clippers' $700,000 fine and the legal strategy
quotes.excerpt: he gets to go and move on in Toronto. So now you're giving me the behind the curtain
quotes.quote: Two things are true. Your instinct of how in the bleep, how in the fill-in-your-profanity, did Kawhi basically skate here is a great question in terms of the merits. He was of course the protagonist. He and his uncle asked for all of it from multiple teams and they got it from the Clippers and he was the guy whose bank account received, according to my reporting, $48 million in total value from Aspiration. That was the contractual value promised, plus now according to the NBA's report, $18 million beyond from three other companies at least, right? That's just through the 2022 time frame and there is more, which I will foreshadow for you. But let's just say $66 million in total value. That's the guy who skated. So why is a political question and answer? And I believe, according to my reporting, that the NBA's incentive this whole time was to make this all end. Can we get this podcast to stop having episodes about this? Can we get the NBA to move on? Can we get people to stop asking about a deeply embarrassing thing for the whole sport?

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Ballmer's reaction to the NBA's ruling
quotes.excerpt: Steve Ballmer has signaled is that he doesn't want to settle. And so what the NBA did
quotes.quote: Steve Ballmer has signaled is that he doesn't want to settle. And so what the NBA did, in lieu of the easy way, is they went a more clever way and they boxed Steve out from arbitration, which prevented the news cycle from lengthening in one regard and gave him one choice, which he can still choose by the way. It just involved discovery and real court and more documents and more questions and a longer timeline and a lot more that we haven't even talked about yet, nor has the NBA. And so that is a question of course for him and his very expensive legal team, which of course we behind the scenes have been getting to know quite well.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Kawhi Leonard's demands and Steve Ballmer's miscalculation
quotes.excerpt: Kawhi Leonard wanted things only Steve Ballmer would give it. What did it cost Steve Ballmer was a calculation
quotes.quote: Kawhi Leonard, say what you will about the legal outcome here for him as a punishment, talk about it as a story, right? I'm not a lawyer, I'm not an outside counsel for the NBA, I'm the guy telling you the story as most transparently as I can. The story has been Kawhi Leonard wanted things only Steve Ballmer would give it. What did it cost Steve Ballmer was a calculation that I believe Steve Ballmer severely messed up. And it becomes 10 first-round picks in totality, it becomes all the things you mentioned, and I think among them by the way, I would highlight banned from his own building that he funded with his own money personally, the most expensive building in the history of American sports, the Intuit Dome, the site of all of this, the nexus of all of these deals. He's banned for a year.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: The Batman analogy for the Clippers' scandal
quotes.excerpt: we're kind of in that scene in Batman, Christopher Nolan's Batman, in which Bane says to his accomplice
quotes.quote: There is insult, there is injury, but now we're kind of in that scene in Batman, Christopher Nolan's Batman, in which Bane says to his accomplice, 'They expect one of us in the wreckage, brother,' and one guy parachutes out of there to Canada and the other one is left holding every bag that we've been describing. And that is also the story of the Kawhi Leonard trade, it's the story of the investigation, it's the story of the ruling we've been waiting 364 days for.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Future investigation targets and Dennis Wong's role
quotes.excerpt: Dennis Wong is the limited partner of the Clippers. Ballmer owns 99%, Dennis Wong owns 1%.
quotes.quote: There are some proper names we've investigated, we continue to investigate. Dennis Wong is the limited partner of the Clippers. Ballmer owns 99%, Dennis Wong owns 1%. He's a character in the Aspiration story, as clear in the financial flow of money that has also been attested to now by the NBA as anybody. No mention of him in the report. For Island Football Club, which is its own rabbit hole here, takes us to the extension Kawhi signed in 2024 in January. The 2024 extension, I will simply say this, was sub-max, less than the max. Given everything we now know about what happened through 22, why would he then take a discount? We continue to report that story and it involves us going to Rhode Island and a second-tier soccer club over there.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Ongoing legal actions and SEC involvement
quotes.excerpt: 11 Aspiration investors have sued Steve Ballmer for fraud because they say if they knew that this whole thing
quotes.quote: Whatever happens in court, as by the way, in civil court in LA where you are, 11 Aspiration investors have sued Steve Ballmer for fraud because they say if they knew that this whole thing was cap circumvention, they would not have invested in the tree-planting startup Aspiration. That proceeds as well. And so there is so much more as by the way, I haven't even mentioned that yesterday on an earnings call, Dectronics, the scoreboard company which got a nine-figure contract from Steve Ballmer because they circumvented the cap for Kawhi Leonard, they have now received requests for information from the SEC. And that is not the Southeastern Conference. That is the Securities and Exchange Commission. And so I'm just saying, I can only get so much information, the NBA can only get so much information. Now the federal government is actively probing this. And so I don't think this is close to over.
